parsed.why: No trans crimes; gender-identity discrimination is criminalised; strong legal protection and visible public acceptance. Anti-LGBT counts are reported suspicions without denominators, not universal visitor-facing restrictions.

Explicit hate-crime and prison-placement protections are traveler-facing. Narrower gender-expression coverage, missing enforcement data, and under-reporting lower certainty, but no documented targeting or facility bans.
Sodomy/public indecency law can reach trans presentation; no recognition, protection, or recourse. State enforcement is older, but armed-group killings and official hostility make discovery severe.

No criminalisation, but absent gender-identity recognition/protection, tiny visibility, religious hostility, and possible service-denial recourse. Risk is mainly social discrimination, not state punishment.

Criminalisation plus advocacy/public-decency enforcement against presentation, police sexual coercion, harsh detention, care denial, and impunity. State-linked targeting of visibly trans people creates severe exposure.
